connector: Has a name ever made you feel something, before you even knew what it meant? In Chapter 7, Mr. Beaver whispers one name, and each of the four children feels something different. Watch how each one feels, and think about why.

a.raw: mr beaver led the children over the dam and they went into his house
a.fixed: Mr. Beaver led the children over the dam, and they went into his house.
a.why: Mr. Beaver is a title and a name, and Mr. ends with a period. A comma goes before and. Led and went are irregular past verbs.

b.raw: mrs beaver was at her sewing machine and she got up to meet them
b.fixed: Mrs. Beaver was at her sewing machine, and she got up to meet them.
b.why: Mrs. Beaver is a title and a name. A comma goes before and. Was and got are irregular past verbs.

cards.title: World Notes: Real Beavers
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Real beavers build dams across streams with sticks, mud and stones.
The dam holds back the water and makes a pond. Beavers live in a home of sticks and mud called a lodge.
Their strong front teeth never stop growing, so chewing wood keeps them the right size.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Mr. Beaver whispers one name, and each child feels something different. Watch how each one feels in Chapter 7.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: two word parts that mean not, verbs that skip -ed, and prefixes.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 7 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you plan a response that compares two characters.

notes.wordParts: The word parts in- and im- both mean not. inactive = not active. impolite = not polite. Use im- before words that start with m or p.
notes.grammar: An irregular verb does not add -ed for the past. You learn each one: say → said, see → saw, sit → sat.
notes.spelling: A prefix goes on the front of a base word, and the base word keeps its spelling. Peel the prefix off to read the base: un + happy.
notes.wgrd: Two characters can see the same moment in different ways. Ask what each one wants, fears or knows.
vocab: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
a statement that something will happen in the future
to be disloyal to someone who trusted you

mods.script: [warmly] Here's this week's reading tip. Two characters can stand in the same room and see it in different ways. Ask what each one wants, fears or knows. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. Mr. Beaver led the children through the snow, and Mrs. Beaver put the kettle on. Led and put never add e d. And a comma comes before and. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See if you were right. Type the base word in each box.
mods.script: [curious] Two little word parts, one big job. The parts at the front of these words both mean not. Inactive means not active. Impolite means not polite. Here's the trick: im comes before words that start with m or p, like polite. Read the four words, and tap See if you were right. Then type the base word hiding in each one.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Sternly. Here's the sentence. Aslan a man, said Mr. Beaver sternly. One, read the sentence: he sounds serious, maybe a little cross. Two, look for word parts: stern, plus l y. Three, check it. Sternly means in a strict, serious way. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the four verbs that should not end in -ed.
mods.script: [warmly] Most verbs add e d for the past. Walk, walked. But some verbs break the rule. Listen. Mr. Beaver catched a fish. Catched? No! It's caught. Verbs like that are called irregular. You learn them one at a time. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find the four verbs that should not end in e d.

mods.todo: Think about the questions. Tap Now name the pattern. Then sort all eight words.
mods.script: Some long words are a short word with an extra part on the front. Replay. Cover the front part. What's left? Play! That front part means again, so replay means play again. Peel off the front, read the base word, then put it back. Tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
